{{Quote|We have them on the run, sir&hellip; They're no match for droidekas.|[[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]], to [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]]|<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
The '''droideka''' (a compound word combining the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] word "[[Droid/Legends|droid]]" with the [[Colicoid (language)/Legends|Colicoid]] suffix ''eka'', meaning "hireling" or "drone"), also called the '''destroyer droid''' ('''destroyers''' for short), '''death balls''', '''wheel droid''', '''roller''', or '''rollies''' in [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] [[List of phrases and slang/Legends#R|slang]], was a type of heavy [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. It gained a reputation for deadliness over the course of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. [[Droid/Legends|Droid]] commanders such as [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] favored the droideka for its resilience and firepower, as well as the fear it could instill in even the most powerful [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. They were also used for executions. They were deployed in many battles over the course of the Clone Wars, such as [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]], usually in moderate numbers due to their cost, and were also used as guards in various Confederate installations. [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] also utilized droidekas as security droids aboard their ships. After the Clone Wars, remaining droidekas fell into the hands of a variety of factions such as [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and criminals.

==Description==
{{Quote|Either that was a very well-kept secret, or else it's something new that someone built into this particular model. It's not all that effective—you saw it could only fire straight along its path, and only at the spot in its rotation when the blasters were turned to the right spot.|Mara Jade Skywalker|<ref name="SQ">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Droideka-CVD.png|thumb|left|A technical diagram of a droideka]]Droidekas were more formidable than the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] more numerous [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] for several reasons. They were able to transform into a "wheel" configuration, allowing rapid movement and compact storage.<ref name="EPIVD" /> When they encountered their targets, each of the [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]]-[[Armor/Legends|armored]] droidekas would unfold into a tripodal weapons platform, armed with a set of two twin [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]] which could unleash a withering torrent of firepower, though some were equipped with a blade weapon on one of the arms, such as a buzzsaw or a vibroblade.<ref name="Republic 29 Hunt for Aurra Sing 2">[[Star Wars (1998) 29|''Star Wars'' (1998) 29]]</ref><ref name="Marked">{{Tales|24|Marked}}</ref> Often, they were also equipped with [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generators]]. These [[Personal energy shield/Legends|personal energy shields]] projected could endure much punishment, capable of deflecting or absorbing virtually any manner of energy or projectile fire up to the level of a light artillery bolt,<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> as well as rebuffing [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] blades and physical attacks.<ref name="EPIVD" /> The shields were powered by a starship-class fusion generator housed in a bulb at the junction of the droideka's legs. However, there was a weak point at the very top of the shield, a point where lightsabers would be able to penetrate. Many Jedi took advantage of this weak point, and it was the most commonly used method of dispatching them in the Clone Wars.<ref name="HoloNet Transmission">{{GamerCite|4|HoloNet Transmission}}</ref> Additionally, the effectiveness of these droids was bolstered by their lack of the usual requirement for [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]]; instead, droidekas utilized [[non-visual composite radiation sensor]]s, which were less likely to be distracted by light-based effects.<ref name="EPIVD" />[[File:Destroyer_droid_sequence.png|thumb|A destroyer droid unfolding]]Before the Federation's defeat following their [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], these droids were usually [[Droid control program|slaved]] to a [[Central Control Computer/Legends|central control computer]].<ref name="EPIVD" /> This technique fell out of favor in the aftermath of said battle, however, and they later functioned independently like the [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]] did.<ref name="AOTC" /> Even before that time, the droidekas on [[Colla IV/Legends|Colla IV]] were not slaved to a central computer, this independence rendering them both much more expensive and much more lethal. What also made them unique to battle droids was that they could roll into position on the battlefield and act as a turret.<ref name="EPIVD" /> Due to their construction and design, they were over 200 times the cost of a regular [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]].<ref name="AOTCVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

[[Droideka dispenser]]s were sometimes used to transport and deploy these droids even in the middle of intense combat zones, proving a serious nuisance to enemy troops.<ref name="SW:RC">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>

==History==
===Pre-Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Master! Destroyers!|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], upon seeing a droideka aboard the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']]|<ref name="TPM" />}}
[[File:AurraSing-swrep29.jpg|thumb|left|Aurra Sing, attacked by droidekas on Talas]]
In [[33 BBY/Legends|32.5 BBY]],<ref>''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> a representative from [[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid Armor Workshop]] recommended the [[Colicoid/Legends|Colicoids]] and their rolling droids to [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]].<ref>''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> 

When the Trade Federation first tested their droid army, they concluded that their centrally controlled infantry performed reasonably well. Some members of the [[Trade Federation Directorate|Trade Federation council]] felt that there needed to be a rapid response droid, able to lay down heavy firepower, small enough to operate in friendly and enemy structures where [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|AATs]] and [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|STAPs]] couldn't go, and able to survive on its own until back-up could arrive. After a debate on the issue of expense, a motion was carried to search for a weapons manufacturer to take on the task. They eventually settled on the [[Colicoid Creation Nest/Legends|Colicoid Creation nest]] of [[Colla IV/Legends|Colla IV]].<ref name=":0">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 5|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 5]] (<small>DRO 1-2: Droideka – Destroyer Droids)</small></ref>

Nute Gunray and the Trade Federation met with the Colicoid Sovereign Nest and bartered fifty bargeloads of exotic flesh in exchange for an exclusive droideka contract. There was some initial strife between the Trade Federation and Colicoids about the design, as the [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoids]] objected to the droids being slaved to a central computer.<ref name=":0" /> Nute Gunray insisted that his droidekas be manufactured without individual intelligence matrices because he didn't trust the Colicoids, and also to knock down the extravagant price.<ref name=":1" /> The designers ultimately relented and quickly delivered the droid. They called the new droid "droideka", combining the word "droid" with the Colicoid suffix for a mindless drone. Most citizens came to call them destroyer droids, for destruction was the stock of their trade. The Colicoids ultimately went on to produce fully independent droidekas for sale on the open market. They knew the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] would be too cowardly to complain in person, and wouldn't go to the courts about a breach in contract regarding the production of an illegal droid.<ref name=":0" />  

The Battle of Naboo marked the first widespread use of the Droidekas, though small batches had previously been deployed to trigger several public atrocities.<ref name=":1">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> One such operation was the Trade Federation's [[Alaris Prime colonial war|attempt]] to annex [[Alaris Prime/Legends|Alaris Prime]] and expel the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] attempting to colonize it, but the Wookiees, with the intervention of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], were able to repulse the Trade Federation forces.<ref name="SWGB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

The Trade Federation utilized large numbers of droidekas during the Invasion of Naboo, where they proved highly effective against Naboo forces. They were used to great effect against two Jedi&mdash;[[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]&mdash;on the flagship [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']], where just two of them forced the Jedi to flee. They were also used during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Grassy Plains]], where they massacred [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] warriors and were responsible for destroying the [[Fambaa/Legends|Fambaa]] shield generators. However, they were disabled when [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] took out the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Droid Control Ship]].<ref name="TPM" /> After the crisis, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] obtained some droidekas from the reparations given to the Trade Federation, and used them onboard ''[[Outbound Flight]]'' as security enforcement, and would be obtained by the Vaagari by this way.<ref name="Outbound Flight">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref>

===Clone Wars===
[[File:Droidekas-Ambush.jpg|thumb|right|Droidekas on Rugosa]]
After the Trade Federation joined the Confederacy of Independent Systems, droidekas became mass-produced in Separatist droid foundries and were a common element of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Confederacy armies]]. They were used in the initial [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], where most of them were stored aboard [[Core ship/Legends|core ships]] which were hence unavailable for the battle, although they were used heavily in the [[Petranaki arena|arena]] stage of the battle.<ref name="AOTC" /> Over the course of the war, they proved extremely effective against enemy [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], with even [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] bearing scars from them<ref name="The Cestus Deception">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref>; they posed a challenge even to elite Republic soldiers such as [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]], as proved aboard ''[[Prosecutor]]''.<ref name="SW:RC" />

They were also sometimes used as bodyguards for high-ranking Separatist figures such as [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]].<ref name="Star Wars: Clone Wars">''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]''</ref> However, they met their match in the [[JK-13 security droid|JK-13]], which was not brought into mass production as the Jedi feared it would be.<ref name="The Cestus Deception" /> Indeed, the mere presence of droidekas was enough to make Jedi or other enemy forces retreat or surrender.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> During the [[Siege of Cato Neimoidia|Battle of Cato Neimoidia]] near the end of the war, squads of droids pinned down a group lead by Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi, and were only destroyed by an [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] strike.<ref name="LOE" />

An unusually large concentration of droidekas were used in the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|assault on Coruscant]], where they were repulsed by [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]].<ref name="Star Wars: Clone Wars" /> In the same battle, droidekas also formed part of the team that captured [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and Kenobi aboard [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], although the Jedi exploited a weakness in their shields during the firefight on the bridge.<ref name="ROTS" />

Unarmed droidekas were used as shooting range targets as part of the training of clone [[Clone sharpshooter/Legends|sharpshooters]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Sharpshooter">{{SWArchive|url=games/playnow/sharpshooter|text=Sharpshooter|int=Sharpshooter (game)}}</ref>

At the end of the Clone Wars, the droidekas were de-activated after [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] execution of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] under [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] orders.<ref name="ROTS" />

===Aftermath===
{{Quote|Yes, the so-called 'destroyer droids' used by the Trade Federation during the Clone Wars. The Empire has a stockpile of the droids and has reprogrammed them to guard various installations across the galaxy, including a research station and the mine here on Lok. The droidekas are programmed to attack anyone who shouldn't be there.|[[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Moore]]|<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies" />}}
[[File:Droideka_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|A droideka provides fire support for a group of stormtroopers.]]
The remaining droidekas were purchased by the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] and other organizations, such as the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], a few system security forces still utilized droidekas. Droidekas were also used by colonies on undeveloped worlds in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] as perimeter guards at night to guard against native predators. In 19 BBY, Droidekas were used by stormtroopers against Jedi Fy-tor Anna. Some fell into the hands of smugglers and criminals, and the [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]] managed to obtain at least one unit.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> During the early years of the Galactic Empire, many droidekas were used by [[Gizor Dellso]] in the [[Battle of Mustafar (Imperial Period)|Battle of Mustafar]]. All were destroyed when the Empire bombarded the planet.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> One was repaired by [[Osaji Uhares]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Triplet Threat">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040122threat|text=Triplet Threat|int=Triplet Threat}}</ref> Around this time, six modified Droidekas were used as the leaders of security [[Squad/Legends|squads]] in [[Aucellis Park]], an entertainment park that was located on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Keriba VI]].<ref name="Beneath Aucellis Park">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030821aucellis|text=Beneath Aucellis Park|int=Beneath Aucellis Park}}</ref> In about [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], the renegade Jedi [[Dal Konur]] obtained some droidekas from a warehouse on [[Wayland/Legends|Wayland]] and he deployed them on [[Bilbringi system/Legends|Bilbringi]].<ref name="RJ">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031023rebel|text=Rebel Jedi|int=Rebel Jedi}}</ref>

[[Tyber Zann]] and [[Urai Fen]] managed to capture an abandoned clone war era droid factory on [[Hypori/Legends|Hypori]] from the automated security droids protecting it. A large [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]] force including [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] and [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] (who was quickly bribed into defecting,) had set a trap for the two crime lords, but Urai was quickly able to reprogram the [[Droideka Mark II|Destroyer Droid MKII]] security force to respond to Tyber, and managed to force Jabba to retreat. After taking [[Hypori/Legends|Hypori]] Zann established many facilities devoted to the manufactore of the these droids to be used as heavy support units for the [[Disruptor/Legends|disruptor]]-armed infantry of the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]].

Due to the strength of their blasters and their built-in shields, droidekas proved to be a serious threat to Jedi, especially when in groups. A few years before the Yuuzhan Vong War, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] encountered a droideka aboard the remains of the ''Outbound Flight'' [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class cruisers]]. Even though it was decades old and not operating at its best, the two still had a difficult time defeating it. However, this version had some interesting additions, one of which was the ability to fire its blasters while in rolling configuration.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" />

==Design flaws==
{{Quote|Data shows that the standard droideka was made with one design flaw: the shields must maintain a continual supply of energy, which may result in an overload if battered enough.|[[TC-38]]|<ref name="Kinect Star Wars">''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''</ref>}}
[[File:DroidekaMK2.jpg|thumb|right|A Mark II variant as part of Tyber Zann's faction fighting in the Galactic Civil War]]
Despite being a formidable droid, the droideka had one major design flaw. Its shield was designed to enclose the droideka in a standing position, but if the droid was knocked on its side or against a wall, the shield had no way of distinguishing the wall or floor from a blaster bolt or lightsaber. This meant that the shield generator had to continue supplying energy to the shield, resulting in an overload, as demonstrated during the rescue on the ''[[Invisible Hand/Legends|Invisible Hand]]''. The shorted-out shield generator would leave the droideka vulnerable. Also, in the rolling position, the droideka's shield could not be activated, leaving it vulnerable while travelling.<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> This technique was demonstrated by Republic Commandos infiltrating a Separatist core ship during the Battle of Geonosis and later by Anakin Skywalker and his [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|padawan]] during the [[Battle of Christophsis/Legends|Battle of Christophsis]]. Furthermore, their shields were substantially weaker behind the droid, making them relatively easy to take out from that position. They also apparently seemed to be vulnerable to Force techniques, as Obi-Wan Kenobi used several to knock out approaching droids (and even slow down General Grievous) on board the CIS superbattleship ''[[Malevolence/Legends|Malevolence]]''.

Droideka shields were ineffective against slow rolling objects, such as [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]] which could be rolled in and detonated. This was taught to the [[Onderon rebels/Legends|Onderon rebels]] by [[Rex/Legends|Captain Rex]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="AWONTF">{{TCW|A War on Two Fronts}}</ref> During the Ringo Vinda campaign they were manipulated by the force and taken down with shields up by an [[Electromagnetic pulse grenade|Electro Magnetic Pulse grenade]]. They also showed little, if any, ability to stop strong explosions as demonstrated when [[Gregor/Legends|Gregor]] encountered them and targeted various barrels of [[Rhydonium/Legends|rhydonium]] in order to destroy them. At the [[Petranaki arena|Geonosis arena]] they were destroyed by Low Altitude Assault Transports with little to no shield resistance;<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref> during the [[Battle of Naboo]], [[Anakin Skywalker]] used the blasters of an [[N-1 starfighter]] to pierce through their shields and destroy three of them.<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|I}}</ref>

Droidekas were known to have a hard time maneuvering on downward slopes and climbing up stairs. In their rolling configuration, they would have to go back quite a bit and then speed up, launching themselves up the stairs. They could also try to traverse stairs in walking configuration, although it was extremely hard for them to coordinate their three legs on stairs. In their standing position, they could not move very fast, forcing them to roll over long distances.<ref name="Battlefront II" />

Additionally, there were limits when a droideka could fire at a target. If the target got very close to it, the droideka would miss its shots because its blaster arms were spread out. This also enabled an enemy to run around it while attacking.<ref name="Battlefront II" />

Lastly, a rather effective method of destroying droidekas was to crush them with a heavy object.

==Droideka series and variants==
[[File:Droideka_grapple.jpg|thumb|left|A Grapple droideka]]
There were three known series of droidekas. They were outwardly similar; the differences were mostly internal. The first, the [[P-series droideka/Legends|P-series droideka]], was used in the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="SWTCG">[[Star Wars Trading Card Game|''Star Wars'' Trading Card Game]]</ref> The [[W-series droideka/Legends|W-series droideka]] was used in the Battle of Geonosis in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="SWTCG" /> Later, the [[Q-series droideka/Legends|Q-series droideka]] was used aboard the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] to capture and trap [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Knight [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="SWTCG" />

Five known variants of droideka existed. The first was the [[grapple droideka]], used around the time of the Invasion of Naboo. It was equipped with electronic grapples and was designed for melee combat, and lacked blasters. It also seemed to possess weaker shields than average.<ref name="Jedi Power Battles">[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'']]</ref>

A second variant was the [[Ultra Droideka]]. These were larger than standard droidekas and saw use during the Clone Wars.<ref name="CloneWarsCampaignGuide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

A third, the [[droideka Mark II]], saw action on the battlefields of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. This model had four stubby legs and an [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]], and was larger than the Separatist models. Since the plans for it were discovered on the old Separatist droid-producing world of [[Hypori/Legends|Hypori]], it may have been a dropped CIS project. It was employed by the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]] briefly, then quite extensively by the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]].<ref name="FOC">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>

A fourth droideka variant was the [[K3-I Buzzer Droid]] used also during the Galactic Civil War. This variant was used on [[Station Gamma]] above [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]]. It was weaker than an average droideka and lacked shields.<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

A fifth droideka was the [[Sniper droideka/Legends|sniper droideka]], which was used by the CIS during the Clone Wars. It included a sniper rifle in its head, in addition to the rest of its weapons. The CIS deployed at least two sniper droideka during its [[Battle of Kiros|invasion]] of [[Kiros/Legends|Kiros]].<ref name="TCWComic1">[[The Clone Wars 1|''The Clone Wars'' 1]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
According to the [[Star Wars home video releases|DVD]] commentary of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], a droideka's blaster is meant to sound similar to those of an [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]]. This is adhered to in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|Episode I game]] and [[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles|''Jedi Power Battles'']] games.<ref name="TPM DVD commentary">{{Film|I}} DVD commentary</ref>

In the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' and its [[2002]] [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns|expansion pack]], destroyer droids are the Trade Federation special unit. They are produced at [[Fortress/Legends|Trade Federation fortresses]] for a cost of 50 units of [[Carbon/Legends|carbon]] and 150 units of [[Nova crystal/Legends|nova crystals]]. Only the upgraded heavy destroyer droid uses shield generators.

Droidekas do not seem to ever use their shields in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] or ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'', and only briefly in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']]. This made them more open to attacks, which was exploited by [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. This is because these are [[W-series droideka/Legends|W-series droideka]], which have more powerful blasters, at the cost of less energy to operate the shields, resulting in the shield being rarely used. This weakness was resolved in the [[Q-series droideka/Legends|Q-series droideka]], which had both powerful blasters and plenty of energy for the shields. The original model, the P-series droideka, had weaker blasters and a slightly less efficient shield than the Q-series.

Early droideka concept art was later used as a basis for the [[LR-57 combat droid/Legends|LR-57 combat droid]] seen in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''The Clone Wars'']] animation. Other concept art had an "alternate take" on the droid with a unicycle mechanism.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref>
